correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs the ring and witness ideal from the stated source hypotheses. Zariski density plus infinite fibers proves \(\iota(A)\cap D=0\). Because every point of \(X\) is nonzero, each coordinate idempotent \(\delta_\omega\) is a multiple of one of \(\iota(x),\iota(y),\iota(z)\), giving \(D\subset I\) and hence \(I=D+\iota(\mathfrak m)\). Finite-support idempotents prove \(D^2=D\), so induction gives \(I^n=D+\iota(\mathfrak m^n)\) for every \(n\ge1\). The quotient, intersection, associated graded, completion, and localization statements then follow by explicit kernels. No finite computation is used to infer an infinite statement.

value.rationale: The result explains where the source's non-McCoy pathology lives. The distinguished ideal is globally faithful and consists entirely of zero-divisors, yet localizing at that very maximal ideal produces the ordinary regular local domain \(k[x,y,z]_{(x,y,z)}\), and every finite \(I\)-adic quotient is the standard truncated polynomial local ring. The exact obstruction is the persistent finite-support tail \(D=\bigcap_{n\ge1}I^n\), making the \(I\)-adic topology nonseparated while leaving the associated graded ring and completion regular. This is a motivated structural refinement of the paper's witness rather than an arbitrary invariant computation.
